  sorry
/- SWARM_PROOF_END -/

/-- Every continuous scalar ODE solution has the exact integrating-factor identity. -/
theorem integratingFactor_identity (q w : ℝ → ℝ) (hq : Continuous q)
    (k s t : ℝ) (hst : s ≤ t) (hw : ContinuousOn w (Icc s t))
    (hd : ∀ x ∈ Ioo s t, HasDerivAt w (-k-q x*w x) x) :
    Real.exp (rateIntegral q s t) * w t =
      w s - k * ∫ x in s..t, Real.exp (rateIntegral q s x) :=
/- SWARM_PROOF_BEGIN -/
by
  sorry
/- SWARM_PROOF_END -/
end PoincareConjecture.ParallelMath
hint: Use the product derivative of exp(rateIntegral)*w on the interior. The derivative is -k*exp(rateIntegral). Apply the FTC on [s,t] with endpoint continuity, or show the derivative of weighted w plus k times its primitive is zero. Handle s=t. This task is independent of the explicit candidate derivative; do not assume the desired integral identity.

/-- Existence, uniqueness on forward times, and monotone dependence on initial width. -/
theorem scalarComparison_solution_interface (q : ℝ → ℝ) (hq : Continuous q)
    (k a s : ℝ) :
    comparisonSolution q k a s s = a ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, HasDerivAt (comparisonSolution q k a s)
      (-k-q t*comparisonSolution q k a s t) t) ∧
    (∀ w : ℝ → ℝ, ContinuousOn w (Ici s) → w s = a →
      (∀ t ∈ Ioi s, HasDerivAt w (-k-q t*w t) t) →
      EqOn w (comparisonSolution q k a s) (Ici s)) ∧
    (∀ a' : ℝ, a ≤ a' → ∀ t : ℝ,
      comparisonSolution q k a s t ≤ comparisonSolution q k a' s t) :=
/- SWARM_PROOF_BEGIN -/
by
  sorry
/- SWARM_PROOF_END -/
end PoincareConjecture.ParallelMath
hint: REDUCE: use all three integrated prerequisites. The identity determines w by division by positive exp(rateIntegral), giving the explicit formula. Monotonicity uses the exact sensitivity and exp positivity. Prove the forward-time restriction exactly; no claim about widths without a geometric evolution estimate.

    ∃ T : ℝ, 0 ≤ T ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, T ≤ t → powerBarrier alpha c a k t < 0 :=

  sorry
/- SWARM_PROOF_END -/

hint: Use divergence of (t+c)^(1-alpha) as t tends to +infinity, since 1-alpha>0. The bracket eventually becomes negative and the prefactor is positive. It is enough to pick an explicit sufficiently large T, but do not incorrectly assert a nonpositive bound is strictly negative. This lemma is a scalar extinction ingredient, not the geometric evolution law.

/-- Frobenius norm controls quadratic evaluation in a finite orthonormal frame. -/
theorem quadraticForm_sq_le {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (A : ι → ι → ℝ) (v : ι → ℝ) :
    (quadraticForm A v)^2 ≤ (∑ i, ∑ j, (A i j)^2) * (∑ i, (v i)^2)^2 :=
/- SWARM_PROOF_BEGIN -/
by
  sorry
/- SWARM_PROOF_END -/
end PoincareConjecture.ParallelMath
hint: Apply finite Cauchy-Schwarz to the double sum against v_i*v_j, then factor sum_{i,j} v_i^2 v_j^2. No symmetry assumption on A. This is the order-zero tensor norm-to-vector estimate needed before epsilon-close can imply metric comparison.

/-- A small coefficient error from the identity gives two-sided quadratic-form bounds. -/
theorem metric_comparison_of_frobenius_error {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (A : ι → ι → ℝ) (epsilon : ℝ) (heps : 0 ≤ epsilon)
    (herror : (∑ i, ∑ j, (A i j - if i=j then 1 else 0)^2) ≤ epsilon^2) :
    ∀ v : ι → ℝ,
      (1-epsilon)*(∑ i, (v i)^2) ≤ quadraticForm A v ∧
      quadraticForm A v ≤ (1+epsilon)*(∑ i, (v i)^2) :=
/- SWARM_PROOF_BEGIN -/
by
  sorry
/- SWARM_PROOF_END -/
end PoincareConjecture.ParallelMath
hint: Use integrated quadraticForm_sq_le on A-Id. Identify its evaluation as quadraticForm A v - sum v_i^2. Take the squared inequality to a two-sided bound, using epsilon>=0 and sum v_i^2>=0. This is a finite-dimensional tensor comparison; it does not itself identify the reference EpsilonClose tensor norm.

import PoincareConjecture.ParallelMath.SurgeryMetric.ChainTriangle
import PoincareConjecture.ParallelMath.SurgeryMetric.GluedMap
import PoincareConjecture.ParallelMath.SurgeryMetric.EpsilonRemoval
import PoincareConjecture.ParallelMath.Core
set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section
namespace PoincareConjecture.ParallelMath
open Set Function Filter
open scoped BigOperators Topology

/-- Gluing local maps is globally Lipschitz when finite piece-chains approximate ambient distance. -/
theorem lipschitz_gluing_of_approximate_piece_chains
    {ι X Y : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] [PseudoMetricSpace Y]
    (S : ι → Set X) (hcover : ∀ x : X, ∃ i, x ∈ S i)
    (f : ι → X → Y) (cost : ι → X → X → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0)
    (hcompat : ∀ i j x, x ∈ S i → x ∈ S j → f i x = f j x)
    (hlocal : ∀ i x y, x ∈ S i → y ∈ S i →
      dist (f i x) (f i y) ≤ (L : ℝ)*cost i x y)
    (hchains : ∀ x y : X, ∀ epsilon : ℝ, 0 < epsilon →
      ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ z : Fin (n+1) → X, ∃ piece : Fin n → ι,
        z 0 = x ∧ z (Fin.last n) = y ∧
        (∀ i, z i.castSucc ∈ S (piece i) ∧ z i.succ ∈ S (piece i)) ∧
        (∑ i : Fin n, cost (piece i) (z i.castSucc) (z i.succ)) ≤ dist x y + epsilon) :
    ∃ F : X → Y, (∀ i x, x ∈ S i → F x = f i x) ∧ LipschitzWith L F :=
/- SWARM_PROOF_BEGIN -/
by
  sorry
/- SWARM_PROOF_END -/
end PoincareConjecture.ParallelMath
hint: REDUCE: use the three integrated map/chain/epsilon lemmas. Glue F from compatibility; for each approximating chain sum local bounds and telescope; then remove epsilon. hchains is an explicit geometric chain approximation hypothesis, not the desired global map bound. The theorem does not assert that any arbitrary finite sphere cut automatically has hchains; that geometric producer remains separate.
